\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ناگهان} (nâgahân)}{ناگهان (nâgahân)}]{\fa{ناگهان} (nâgahân) — suddenly, all of a sudden}

\label{lesson:FA-C300-nagahan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an invoice, then the Persian for a cash machine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ناگهان}}
\textbf{\fa{ناگهان}} (\emph{nâgahân}) — \textquotedblleft{}suddenly, all of a sudden\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ناگهان} \fa{برق} \fa{رفت} \fa{و} \fa{خانه} \fa{تاریک} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Nâgahân barq raft va khâne târik shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Suddenly the power went off and the house went dark.
\end{quote}

Neutral and common in stories; in everyday speech Iranians also say \emph{yekhow}. It usually opens the clause.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nâgahân} is inherited: EtymDB derives it from \emph{nâgah} (also \emph{nâgâh}), which continues Middle Persian \emph{anāgāh}, \textquotedblleft{}unaware, unwitting\textquotedblright{}. A sudden thing comes on you unawares.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nâgahân}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nâgahân}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{nâgahân}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an invoice, then the Persian for a cash machine, then say \emph{nâgahân} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بلافاصله} (belâfâsele)}{بلافاصله (belâfâsele)}]{\fa{بلافاصله} (belâfâsele) — immediately, right away}

\label{lesson:FA-C300-belafasele}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a cash machine, then the Persian for suddenly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بلافاصله}}
\textbf{\fa{بلافاصله}} (\emph{belâfâsele}) — \textquotedblleft{}immediately, right away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پلیس} \fa{بلافاصله} \fa{به} \fa{محل} \fa{رسید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Polis belâfâsele be mahal resid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police arrived at the scene immediately.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}without a gap\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Belâfâsele ba'd az} means \textquotedblleft{}right after\textquotedblright{}: \emph{belâfâsele ba'd az shâm} \textquotedblleft{}right after dinner\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{belâfâsele} is an Arabic phrase taken over whole: \emph{bi-} \textquotedblleft{}with\textquotedblright{}, \emph{lā} \textquotedblleft{}no\textquotedblright{} and \emph{fāṣila} \textquotedblleft{}an interval, a gap\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists Arabic \emph{fāṣila}). Persian uses it as a single adverb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{belâfâsele}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{belâfâsele}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{belâfâsele}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a cash machine, then the Persian for suddenly, then say \emph{belâfâsele} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{بلافاصله} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Immediately, right away\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بی} \fa{درنگ} (bi derang)}{بی درنگ (bi derang)}]{\fa{بی} \fa{درنگ} (bi derang) — without delay, at once}

\label{lesson:FA-C300-bi-derang}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for suddenly, then the Persian for immediately.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بی} \fa{درنگ}}
\textbf{\fa{بی} \fa{درنگ}} (\emph{bi derang}) — \textquotedblleft{}without delay, at once\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{بی} \fa{درنگ} \fa{به} \fa{آمبولانس} \fa{زنگ} \fa{زد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U bi derang be âmbulâns zang zad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She called an ambulance without delay.
\end{quote}

Formal and literary; in speech \emph{fowran} or \emph{zud} is more usual. Built from \emph{bi} \textquotedblleft{}without\textquotedblright{} and \emph{derang} \textquotedblleft{}delay\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bi derang} is built from \emph{bi} \textquotedblleft{}without\textquotedblright{} and \emph{derang} \textquotedblleft{}a delay, a pause\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Middle Persian \emph{dērang}, \textquotedblleft{}a period, a duration\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bi derang}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bi derang}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bi derang}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for suddenly, then the Persian for immediately, then say \emph{bi derang} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{همین} \fa{که} (hamin ke)}{همین که (hamin ke)}]{\fa{همین} \fa{که} (hamin ke) — the moment that, as soon as}

\label{lesson:FA-C300-hamin-ke}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for immediately, then the Persian for without delay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{همین} \fa{که}}
\textbf{\fa{همین} \fa{که}} (\emph{hamin ke}) — \textquotedblleft{}the moment that, as soon as\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{همین} \fa{که} \fa{در} \fa{را} \fa{باز} \fa{کردم،} \fa{گربه} \fa{فرار} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hamin ke dar râ bâz kardam, gorbe farâr kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The moment I opened the door, the cat ran away.
\end{quote}

It opens a clause, with the past for a past event: \emph{hamin ke residam} \textquotedblleft{}as soon as I arrived\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hamin ke} joins \emph{hamin} \textquotedblleft{}this very\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{ham} \textquotedblleft{}same, also\textquotedblright{} and \emph{in} \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{}, with the linking word \emph{ke} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}. All of its parts are inherited Persian words.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hamin ke}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hamin ke}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{hamin ke}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for immediately, then the Persian for without delay, then say \emph{hamin ke} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اتفاقی} (ettefâqi)}{اتفاقی (ettefâqi)}]{\fa{اتفاقی} (ettefâqi) — by chance, accidentally}

\label{lesson:FA-C300-ettefaqi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for without delay, then the Persian for the moment that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اتفاقی}}
\textbf{\fa{اتفاقی}} (\emph{ettefâqi}) — \textquotedblleft{}by chance, accidentally\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دیروز} \fa{اتفاقی} \fa{دوست} \fa{مدرسه} \fa{ام} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{بازار} \fa{دیدم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Diruz ettefâqi dust-e madrese-am râ dar bâzâr didam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Yesterday I ran into my school friend at the bazaar by chance.
\end{quote}

Also an adjective: \emph{yek didâr-e ettefâqi} \textquotedblleft{}a chance meeting\textquotedblright{}. Built on \emph{ettefâq} \textquotedblleft{}an event\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ettefâqi} adds the Persian suffix \emph{-i} to \emph{ettefâq} \textquotedblleft{}an event\textquotedblright{}, which is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ittifāq} (EtymDB). In Arabic the word is usually glossed \textquotedblleft{}agreement, coincidence\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
